import math

# Borrowings from the public - Federal securities (in millions of dollars)
# From 2020 bulletin (FY2016-2020) and 2024 bulletin (FY2021-2024)
data = {
    2016: 1419286,
    2017: 666472,
    2018: 1258348,
    2019: 1208690,
    2020: 4234396,
    2021: 1484000,
    2022: 2453245,
    2023: 2150233,
    2024: 2241060
}

# Sort values
values = sorted(data.values())
print("Borrowings from the public - Federal securities (millions of dollars):")
for year, val in sorted(data.items()):
    print(f"FY{year}: {val:,}")

print("\nSorted values:")
print(values)

# Compute natural logs
logs = [math.log(v) for v in values]
print("\nNatural logs:")
for i, (v, l) in enumerate(zip(values, logs)):
    print(f"{v}: ln({v}) = {l:.6f}")

# 20% trimmed mean: with 9 values, 20% = 1.8, so we trim 1 from each end (or 2?)
# Standard approach: trim floor(p*n) from each end
# floor(0.2 * 9) = floor(1.8) = 1 from each end, leaving 7 values

n = len(values)
trim_pct = 0.20
trim_count = int(n * trim_pct)
print(f"\nn = {n}, trim_pct = {trim_pct}, trim_count = {trim_count}")

trimmed_logs = logs[trim_count:-trim_count]
print(f"Trimmed logs (removing {trim_count} from each end):")
print(trimmed_logs)

# Calculate mean of trimmed data
trimmed_mean = sum(trimmed_logs) / len(trimmed_logs)
print(f"\n20% trimmed mean of ln(values): {trimmed_mean:.6f}")
print(f"Rounded to 3 decimal places: {trimmed_mean:.3f}")
EOF
